definition: Grokipedia is an AI-generated online encyclopedia operated by the American company xAI, founded by Elon Musk.
details: The site was launched on October 27, 2025. Some entries are generated by Grok, a large language model owned by the same company (xAI), while others were forked from Wikipedia, with some altered and some used nearly verbatim. Articles cannot be directly edited, though logged-in visitors to the encyclopedia can suggest new articles or corrections via a pop-up form, which are reviewed by Grok, and Grok makes autonomous changes to articles. At launch, Musk suggested Grokipedia would strip the "woke" content out of Wikipedia and act as an alternative to that site. Musk has previously described Wikipedia as an "extension of legacy media propaganda". External analysis of Grokipedia's content has focused on its accuracy and biases due to hallucinations and potential algorithmic bias, which reviewers have described as promoting right-wing perspectives and Musk's views. The majority of coverage has described the website as validating, promoting, and legitimizing a variety of debunked conspiracy theories and ideas against scientific consensus on topics such as HIV/AIDS denialism, vaccines and autism, climate change, and race and intelligence. explainer.lead: Grokipedia is an online encyclopedia, launched by xAI on October 27, 2025, that combines articles generated by Grok with material forked from Wikipedia. Its AI-controlled editing process has prompted scrutiny of its accuracy, political bias, and treatment of debunked claims.

tiers.eli5: Imagine an encyclopedia where a robot writes some pages, copies and changes others from an older encyclopedia, and is the only one allowed to make edits. Readers can send notes about mistakes, but the robot decides what changes to make. That is roughly how Grokipedia works, so its pages still need careful checking.
tiers.practitioner: Treat Grokipedia as an AI-mediated reference source rather than a directly editable collaborative encyclopedia. Account for its mixed provenance—Grok-generated text, altered Wikipedia forks, and near-verbatim copies—and for reported risks including hallucinations, algorithmic bias, and claims contrary to scientific consensus.
tiers.paperLevel: Grokipedia is an xAI-operated online encyclopedia whose corpus combines Grok-generated entries with Wikipedia-derived entries, some altered and some nearly verbatim. Its update mechanism is centralized and AI-mediated: visitors submit suggestions, Grok reviews them, and Grok autonomously modifies articles. External reviewers have raised concerns about hallucinations, algorithmic bias, right-wing and Musk-aligned perspectives, and the legitimization of debunked claims concerning HIV/AIDS, vaccines and autism, climate change, and race and intelligence.

explainer.example: A logged-in reader finds a problem in an article derived from Wikipedia and submits a correction through the pop-up form. Grok reviews the suggestion and makes any resulting change; the reader cannot edit the article directly.

usedIn.name: xAI
usedIn.detail: Operates Grokipedia and owns the Grok model used in its content and editing process.

usedIn.name: Online reference publishing
usedIn.detail: Presents an AI-generated and AI-edited alternative to Wikipedia.

explainer.intuition: The core idea is to replace direct community editing with AI-generated content and AI-mediated revisions. Human readers can propose changes, but Grok controls the resulting edits.
howItWorks: Other entries are forked from Wikipedia, either altered or copied nearly verbatim.
Logged-in visitors suggest articles or corrections through a pop-up form.
Grok reviews the suggestions and autonomously changes articles.
explainer.whyItMatters: Grokipedia shows how an encyclopedia can delegate both authorship and editorial control to an AI system. That makes its hallucinations, potential algorithmic bias, and promotion of claims against scientific consensus important concerns for readers.
misconceptions: Not every article is generated by Grok; many are derived from Wikipedia.
Logged-in visitors can suggest changes but cannot edit articles directly.
Copying Wikipedia material does not mean every copied entry remains unchanged.
